summary: The candidate is a meaningful partial improvement to initial single-rank diffusion pipeline loading, and its focused tests pass. It does not fully implement or verify the original issue: native from_pretrained component loads are serialized by a lock covering the entire native load, Qwen-Image cold-start was not exercised, refit/wake-up paths are unchanged, production pageable-memory loading is unchanged, and multi-rank loading is explicitly sequential. Request changes so the scope and tests match the original contract or the contribution is clearly narrowed and the native-load serialization is corrected.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before reproduction of the loading contract: three top-level component loads were sequential (max_active=1, elapsed 0.452 s for three 0.15 s loads).

Candidate regression and compatibility suite: 31 passed. Most overlap coverage mocks PipelineComponentLoader.load_component and therefore does not establish overlap through real native from_pretrained paths.
Independent top-level overlap control: mocked components overlapped (max_active=3, elapsed 0.152 s).

Independent adversarial counterexample: two native loads entering _load_native_with_context were serialized (max_active_native_loads=1, elapsed 0.401 s for two 0.20 s loads) because model_construction_lock wraps the complete load_native/from_pretrained call.

One AMD MI355X executed three mocked concurrently transferred Linear modules and matched NumPy. This validates GPU execution and arithmetic only, not a real diffusion checkpoint loader or Qwen-Image semantics.
Extended compatibility: 68 passed and 9 subtests passed.

gpu_execution.evidence: Assigned AMD Instinct MI355X (gfx950:sramecc+:xnack-), one visible GPU, Torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2, HIP 7.2.26015. The candidate's mocked Linear/NumPy numerical test passed. No Qwen-Image weights or end-to-end serving run was available.

remaining_counterexamples: Two native transformers/diffusers component loads do not overlap: _load_native_with_context holds model_construction_lock across the full load_native call, and load_native calls from_pretrained including checkpoint I/O and weight materialization.
The reported Qwen-Image 63.20-second module-load bottleneck and launch-time reduction were not reproduced or measured with real model weights.
Sleep/wake restoration and post-training refit paths are not changed or tested, despite being part of the original requested benefit.
Production checkpoint mappings remain pageable; the pinned-memory concern raised in the issue is measured only by an unrelated transfer microbenchmark and is not fixed.
Multi-rank component loading remains sequential by design, so the feature does not cover distributed launches.
Peak host-memory behavior under concurrent real checkpoint loading is neither bounded automatically nor measured with representative weights.
remaining_limitations: No Qwen/Qwen-Image weights were present, so architecture-specific loading, numerical correctness, peak memory, and end-to-end cold-start speedup remain unverified.
Only one AMD MI355X (gfx950) was assigned; CUDA/NVIDIA behavior and multi-GPU execution were unavailable.
The tiny Llama serving fixture is not applicable evidence for a diffusion architecture and was not used.
No native C++, HIP, FlyDSL, or generated native source changed in the candidate; native rebuild was not applicable. Imports resolved to /job/repo/python/sglang and the pinned prepared interpreter.
NUMA balancing was enabled on the node; it was not changed because node-wide state changes were outside scope.
